evidence: M-O s.v. Gregorian chant: cantus Grēgoriānus, after Du Cange’s cantus ecclēsiasticus
terms.comment: Church chant is cantus ecclēsiasticus (Du Cange), the Western plainchant cantus Grēgoriānus (M-O; the ē is the eta of Greek Γρηγόριος); the Byzantine and Slavonic chant of the Orthodox Church has no Latin name in these sources.

evidence: Ambr. hymn. Deus creātor 12: hymnum canentēs solvimus

terms.comment: Classically to play the cithara, or sing to it (Sall. Cat. 25.2; Hor.).

phrases.latin: Cantābō Dominō in vītā meā; psallam Deō meō quamdiū sum.
phrases.english: I will sing to the Lord all my life; I will sing psalms to my God while I live.

sources: Lewis & Short: cantus · Lewis & Short: cano · Lewis & Short: psallo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Gregorian chant.
